verdict.rationale: Figma's REST API supports personal access tokens, OAuth (which lets requests be made without using a personal account) and organization/enterprise-scoped 'plan access tokens' (figma-docs-48, figma-docs-57, figma-docs-66), and the hosted remote MCP server enforces an OAuth flow with a distinct 'mcp:connect' scope (figma-probe-rt-2), showing some credential scoping exists for agent access. However there is no documentation of fine-grained, least-privilege permission sets (e.g., read-only vs write-only, per-resource scopes) specifically for issuing to an AI agent, so it falls short of a full least-privilege credential system. Missing for 10: granular per-capability scopes (read/write/file-specific) for agent tokens, explicit docs on creating restricted-scope credentials for AI agents, and independent confirmation of scope enforcement in practice.
